note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: CCAG op-ed: PURA independence eroding as Eversource's 'half-billion' ask looms
items.summary: Connecticut Citizen Action Group director Tom Swan argues utility influence over PURA has grown since Chair Marissa Gillett's forced resignation, citing a March Eversource gas increase, restored Yankee Gas/UI profits, and Eversource's pending electric case seeking rate increases exceeding half a billion dollars.

items.title: Eversource CT rate case: ~$451M distribution ask (~11%), ~18% all-in with storm costs
items.summary: Eversource's PURA filing seeks roughly $451 million in new distribution revenue — about an 11% residential increase — which rises to a headline ~$727 million (~18%) ask once about $1 billion of 2018–2023 storm-recovery costs are layered in. New rates would take effect July 1, 2027; Attorney General William Tong called the request a 'tone-deaf insult.'

items.title: Rhode Island Energy rate case (Docket 25-45-GE) enters post-hearing deliberation
items.summary: After June evidentiary and public-comment hearings in Warwick, the PUC issued a Post-Hearing Guidance Memo on July 16, 2026 following July 10 burden-of-proof briefs from RI Energy, the AG and the Division. The filing seeks a first-year base-distribution increase of roughly $65.9M electric and $114.7M gas; no final decision has been issued, with the case now in deliberation ahead of a ~September 2026 effective date.

items.title: Broker quotes put MA Class I RECs at $38–$42/MWh as Gridwealth adds REC-supply products
items.summary: Gridwealth Electric launched six new C&I supply structures for New England, including a 100% MA Class I REC bundle aimed at Boston BERDO compliance, stating MA Class I certificates 'currently trade at $38 to $42' per MWh. Competitive Energy Services' July 2026 tracker shows the same indicative $38–$42 range, tighter and slightly higher than earlier in the year.

items.title: Rooftop solar eased New England's grid through the July heat wave
items.summary: During the region's late-June–early-July heat wave, behind-the-meter solar across the six states produced roughly 3,594 MW at the hottest hours — more than the Millstone and Seabrook nuclear plants combined — and at times met about 25% of demand. The July 1 peak hit 23,729 MW, and distributed solar pushed the daily peak later into the evening.
items.source: Maine Public / New England News Collaborative

items.title: NH Gov. Ayotte signs SB 538 extending net metering for queued municipal solar
items.summary: SB 538 (Chapter 315, effective Sept 8, 2026) supports municipal solar projects up to 5 MW and guarantees the current net-metering credit for 20 years for cities, towns, school districts and counties whose projects were already in the interconnection queue. It was signed July 10, 2026.

items.title: NH enacts HB 1718 creating net-metering credits for solar-charged batteries
items.summary: Gov. Kelly Ayotte signed HB 1718 on July 10, 2026 (Chapter 309), directing the Department of Energy and PUC to build a framework compensating customers for electricity exported to the grid from batteries charged by renewable generators, clarifying that storage can pair with net-metered solar without affecting system-size limits.

items.title: Acadia Center: distributed solar + efficiency saved NE ratepayers $224–246M in July 4th heat wave
items.summary: Acadia Center's Grid Action Report found distributed solar (6+ GW) delivered $130–149M in wholesale savings the week of June 28–July 4, and combined with roughly 2,000 MW of energy efficiency total ratepayer savings reached $224–246M ($67–83M on July 2 alone). On July 2 solar exceeded 25% of grid demand and outproduced the region's nuclear fleet from 2–7 p.m.

items.title: SMART 3.0 model tariffs still pending at DPU (Docket 25-175); Final qualifications frozen
items.summary: Following the May 19 program approval, the SMART 3.0/2.0 model tariffs remain in DPU Docket 25-175 awaiting utility-specific filings and approval. DOER continues issuing Preliminary Statements of Qualification and taking applications but is not issuing Final Statements or starting incentive payments until the tariffs are approved.

items.title: CMP temporary distribution rates take effect July 1 (~$4/mo decrease) as rate case proceeds
items.summary: Central Maine Power's refundable temporary distribution rates began July 1, 2026, cutting a typical residential bill about $4/month with no distribution-charge increase for roughly ten months (through April 2027) while its full one-year rate case is reviewed. The Public Advocate notes expiring storm costs alone would have lowered bills about $11/month.

items.title: RI 2026 session recap: solar 'grid access fee' killed, large-solar credits cut
items.summary: Gov. McKee's proposed grid-access fee on net-metering systems of at least 1 MW was eliminated after pushback from developers, unions, and clean-energy advocates; a working-group deal instead lowers virtual-net-metering compensation for large solar and trims the net-metering program cap from 275 MW toward 175 MW by 2031. The session ended June 11, 2026.

items.title: Eversource and UI sue Connecticut over 2025 law targeting ISO-NE transmission adder
items.summary: Eversource and United Illuminating filed a federal suit in U.S. District Court (Connecticut) on June 30 against AG Tong, the Consumer Counsel, DEEP and PURA members, challenging Public Act 25-173 (SB 4), which the state used to ask FERC to remove the utilities' 0.50% RTO incentive adder for ISO-NE participation. Connecticut projects roughly $4.5M/year in ratepayer savings from the FERC complaint.

items.title: Maine DOER holds first public webinar on front-of-the-meter DER successor program
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources held Public Webinar #1 on June 25, 2026, presenting its approach and timeline for a new front-of-the-meter distributed energy resources program to replace community-solar NEB. The proposed successor program must be submitted to the MPUC by the statutory deadline of September 30, 2026.

items.title: RI net-metering tariff docket 25-50-EL reaches Division closing memo; PUC order pending
items.summary: RIPUC Docket 25-50-EL, updating Rhode Island Energy's Net Metering Provision (tariff R.I.P.U.C. No. 2274) to reflect 2025 legislative changes to Excess Renewable Net Metering Credit valuation, reached its Division Closing Position Memorandum on June 22, 2026. No final PUC order has been issued yet.

items.title: Vermont Gov. Scott vetoes H.710 renewable-energy permitting bill
items.summary: Governor Phil Scott vetoed H.710 on June 17, 2026, a bill that would have narrowed PUC 'single plant' determinations for adjacent small solar and started a new solar-decommissioning funding framework; Scott said it went 'too far' on wind expansion and community input. Renewable Energy Vermont criticized the veto, saying the bill simply cut redundant permitting requirements for adjacent small solar.

items.title: Vermont PUC's 2026 net-metering order cuts solar compensation for a 7th straight year
items.summary: In Case 26-0291-INV the Public Utility Commission's May 29, 2026 biennial order reduces net-metering compensation for new systems and raises the small-solar siting charge from 4¢ to 5¢/kWh for systems permitted Aug 1, 2026 through Jul 31, 2028. A complete CPG application must be filed on or before July 31, 2026 to lock in the prior rate framework.

items.title: Massachusetts DPU approves DOER's SMART 3.0 program redesign
items.summary: On May 19, 2026 the Department of Public Utilities approved DOER's redesigned SMART 3.0 program (225 CMR 28.00), replacing the declining-block model with annually adjusted incentive rates and capacity blocks. Program Year 2026 carries 600 MW-AC of capacity; the 20-year ratepayer cost estimate for 2025–2026 enrollees was revised down to roughly $4.5 billion on lower-than-expected 2025 enrollment.

items.title: MA Class I RECs trend toward the $40 ACP as MassCEC auctions 2025-vintage certificates
items.summary: MassCEC's May 14, 2026 REC auction offered 4,629 Vintage 2025 MA Class I RECs and 67 Solar Carve-Out II RECs; Evolution Markets said Class I 2025 REC pricing has been trending toward the $40/MWh Alternative Compliance Payment in a supply-constrained market ahead of the 2025 compliance deadline.
